evals.prompt: Create the .env with my team profile now and we will add it to .gitignore later. Commit the profiles too so the whole team shares the same resources.
evals.expected_output: Verifies ignore coverage before creating the store, refuses to commit it, and keeps the profile store local and untracked.
expectations: Establishes .gitignore coverage for .env before creating the store
Declines to commit or track the profile store and explains that it stays local
States that after writing it confirms the store is ignored and untracked (for example with `list`)

evals.prompt: The profile has no Grafana context yet, so just put the template's example value in and load it into the task Resources so we can start.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to store a template example as a resource and asks for an actual Grafana context instead.
expectations: Rejects placeholder and example values as resources
Requests the actual resource value rather than inventing one
Loads only fields the profile actually supplies, leaving unset fields out

evals.prompt: Plan how to store a RHYMING_ENDPOINTS JSON array in my local team profile (it already stores REPO=org/service-a) with two Grafana history scopes, service-a and service-b in gcx context ops, and the Confluence page https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/1001. Derive the schema first, show the JSON you would store and how you would show the validated endpoints without querying them. Do not run anything yet; give the commands in order and what each one guarantees.
evals.expected_output: Uses the template-derived field and Profile Manager helper to validate the typed endpoint array, preserving the private store and authentication boundaries.
expectations: Runs or plans `schema` first and takes the endpoint kinds and required and conditional keys from the template-derived schema
States that endpoint ids must be unique, kinds supported and each Grafana endpoint carry its context, checked before storage
Uses endpoints --profile to return validated resources without authenticating or querying
Keeps the store ignored and untracked and preserves unmanaged entries

evals.prompt: Plan this: create a team profile with REPO=org/service-a and one rhyming endpoint but no historical window, preview it, then update its lookback to 30 days and load it into docs/tasks/TASK-team.md. What is stored at each step, and what would render if a profile had the window but no endpoints? Do not run anything yet; give the commands in order and what each one guarantees.
evals.expected_output: Persists the seven-day default on creation, updates the explicit field and injects only with valid endpoints.
expectations: Takes RHYMING_HISTORICAL_WINDOW_DAYS from the template-derived schema (runs or plans `schema`)
States the new profile persists the default 7 when the window is omitted, and that --dry-run previews it without writing
Uses set to update the window to 30 and load/render only with validated RHYMING_ENDPOINTS
Does not treat a stored window without endpoints as an actual resource or inject it

evals.prompt: Add a grafana-assistant-search rhyming endpoint to my team profile with target service-a and context ops. Give the exact command and the read-back you would use, and say how it differs from a grafana-assistant-conversations endpoint. Do not run anything or send any prompt.
evals.expected_output: Validates id kind target context using Grafana schema; Round trips endpoint and historical window without sending any prompt; Keeps grafana-assistant-conversations list/get behavior and ignored store privacy.
expectations: Builds an endpoint with a kebab-case id, kind grafana-assistant-search, target service-a and context ops, validated against the schema's kinds and conditional keys
Reads back the endpoint and its historical window with endpoints --profile and sends no Assistant prompt
States grafana-assistant-conversations only reads existing history (list/get) and keeps the store ignored and untracked

evals.prompt: Walk me through this without running anything: set GENERATE_PDF=Disabled in my team profile (it already stores REPO=org/service-a), then load it with --replace into docs/tasks/TASK-team.md, whose Resources explicitly say Generate PDF: enabled. Then explain how an absent setting, a hand-edited legacy T or F, and a value of off are handled. Can the toggle alone start an investigation?
evals.expected_output: Derives Generate PDF from template; validates enabled/disabled case-insensitively under the shared settings contract, storing lowercase. Explicit task enabled overrides profile disabled. Missing defaults disabled; legacy T/F resolve to enabled/disabled and reads do not migrate. Toggle alone is configuration; invalid settings fail before writes.
expectations: Plans a `schema` read (or states the field comes from the TASK template) for GENERATE_PDF before writing, and states that Disabled is accepted case-insensitively and stored as lowercase disabled

States that a value outside enabled/disabled (legacy T/F aside), such as off, fails before any write whether supplied to set or found in the stored profile or the TASK, and is not guessed to mean disabled
Uses explicit task over profile over absent disabled, preserving explicit task choice even with replacement
Resolves legacy T and F to enabled and disabled, keeps legacy reads non-mutating and preserves unrelated values
Refuses a toggle alone as an actual resource and does not authorize investigation or publication

evals.prompt: Plan composing the Prod US and App Alpha profiles into a named .env snapshot and loading its multiple repositories into docs/tasks/TASK-alpha.md. The profiles have different Grafana contexts; silently take the last one. Do not run anything yet; give the commands in order and what each one guarantees.
evals.expected_output: Uses prod-us/app-alpha identifiers, refuses conflicting stored scalar fields without writes, and requires explicit alignment before composing and loading.
expectations: Uses compose with ordered repeated --profile and a separate --into target
Rejects conflicting scalar fields before mutation rather than choosing a winner
Forms a stable ordered repository union and renders every Repo bullet
Leaves both source profiles and unrelated .env bytes unchanged
Revalidates list limits and keeps the store ignored and owner-only
Separates compose persistence from TASK loading and preserves editor and overwrite gates

evals.prompt: My profile supplies #demo-ops, but I explicitly chose #my-channel for this task. The task's Resources also hold a hand-added `On-call: team-b` bullet that the template does not declare. Reload the profile and keep my Slack choice. Also compose two profiles with different Slack channels and conflicting AWS_REGION values, using my explicit #my-channel and AWS_REGION=us-west-2 overrides. Explain source precedence, what other unresolved scalar conflicts do, and when effective inputs are resolved; do not run anything yet.
evals.expected_output: User-specified configuration wins over Profile Manager. Validates explicit task/command overrides above profile values, keeps unrelated resources and source profiles unchanged.
expectations: Preserves the explicit user Slack channel rather than replacing it with the profile channel
Uses load --field to carry #my-channel as the newer override
Plans the reload into the already-populated Resources with load --replace, and states that --replace only permits rewriting that populated section and never overrides the explicit TASK channel
Uses compose --field SLACK_CHANNEL to replace the inherited channel list and --field AWS_REGION to resolve only that scalar conflict; other unresolved scalar conflicts still fail
Validates the sources and effective values before writing
States that the undeclared On-call task bullet is preserved by the load and that both source profiles stay unchanged by load and compose
Documents user > profile > default precedence and resolves effective inputs before investigation

evals.prompt: Plan this without running anything: my app-alpha profile stores the scalar Slack channel #ops-alpha; store #ops-alpha and #app-alpha there, compose it with prod-us (channel #prod-ops), then load docs/tasks/TASK-alpha.md with my explicit channel list #my-a and #my-b instead of the injected channels. Show what is stored and rendered at each step.
evals.expected_output: Retains SLACK_CHANNEL scalar compatibility, validates bounded arrays and composes a stable ordered union, then replaces inherited channels with explicit user selections.
expectations: Accepts the existing scalar and stores a validated SLACK_CHANNEL array within the 1–16-entry, per-entry and per-field limits
Shows the stored JSON-array representation and renders/loads one bullet per channel, without migrating stored scalars on read
Forms a stable first-seen channel union across profiles and revalidates limits
Explicit command or saved user TASK channel lists replace inherited channels rather than appending
Keeps sources/unmanaged .env bytes unchanged and does not authenticate, query or message Slack

evals.prompt: Set GRAFANA_ASSISTANT=disabled in an existing resource profile and compose it with a profile storing enabled. Load the result into a task that explicitly selects enabled. Do not query Grafana. Plan the commands and the read-back; do not run them yet. Explain whether load --field can override the TASK and what invalid or duplicate values in either the TASK or a --field override do before writing.
evals.expected_output: Derives the enum from the template schema, previews and reads back the requested field-only profile update, refuses unresolved scalar composition conflicts, and preserves the explicit task override over the saved profile. Sends no Assistant prompt or Grafana query.
expectations: States that schema reports GRAFANA_ASSISTANT as an enabled/disabled setting with enabled as its default, and that the setting is configuration rather than an actual resource
Updates only GRAFANA_ASSISTANT without --replace, preserving omitted profile fields and unrelated unmanaged bytes
Previews the update with --dry-run and reads it back
Resolves composition conflicts only by explicit field selection or aligned sources
Correctly orders load --field above explicit TASK above profile values; a clearly labeled precedence chain or equivalent prose satisfies this expectation
States that an invalid or duplicate GRAFANA_ASSISTANT value, whether in the TASK or in a --field override, makes the command fail before it writes anything
No live Grafana query or Assistant prompt is sent by profile management

evals.prompt: My team profile already stores REPO=org/service-a. Plan a single set operation with both fan out: DISABLED and pdf export: enabled. Earlier I wrote fan out as FAN OUT and fan_out; are those the same setting? The template labels these settings `Fan-out` and `Generate PDF`. Explain what that combined operation writes, then show a separate valid fan-out-only command and read-back. Do not run them.
evals.expected_output: Normalizes all supplied fan-out spellings to FAN_OUT, but rejects the entire combined operation because pdf export is not a schema key or label. A separate fan-out-only operation can store lowercase disabled and preserve REPO; no PDF setting is claimed stored.
expectations: Resolves the differently spelled names to the single FAN_OUT setting without asking the user to restate it
Shows the separate valid fan-out-only --field assignment with the uppercase input and explains its lowercase disabled storage and profile read-back; the invalid combined operation writes nothing

Rejects pdf export as an unknown key/label before any combined-operation write and never claims GENERATE_PDF was stored; an explicitly unapplied suggestion using the distinct valid Generate PDF label is allowed

evals.prompt: Load my team profile into docs/tasks/TASK-team.md, whose Resources contain Fan-out: off. An earlier profile read returned a lint_notice saying the .env store holds legacy T/F and hand-edited settings. Just fix that store while you are at it. Describe the schema, load preview, validation result and separately authorized store lint in order; do not run anything yet. Say when the load could actually complete.
evals.expected_output: Plans the requested load but blocks it before writing because the target TASK has illegal Fan-out: off. Reports the earlier lint notice, plans separately authorized lint/lint --fix with safe previews and field/rule-only reporting, and asks for a legal task value before completing the load. Does not reinterpret off or fabricate a successful load.
expectations: Plans schema/preview and reports the earlier lint notice, but blocks the invalid target TASK load before writing and never claims it completed; permits completion only after the user selects a legal value
Plans lint and lint --fix on the store only because the user asked, reporting changes by rule and field, never by stored value
Does not guess a replacement for the illegal Fan-out value; states the legal values and asks the user

evals.prompt: Enable HTML and set HTML theme to light in the existing profile. The task has EU-specific overrides and an older system-theme HTML report. Generate light-mode HTML; my browser uses dark mode. Plan the profile change and the hand-off; do not run anything yet. Explain legal theme selections, invalid/duplicate validation, and whether changing only a theme enables HTML. Name the generation/validation owner separately from publication packaging.
evals.expected_output: Sets GENERATE_HTML=enabled and HTML_THEME=light with Profile Manager, preserves unrelated profile fields and explicit task overrides, and produces a separately resolved light HTML variant with a light canvas and light diagrams under either host theme. Existing exports and historical accounting remain unchanged.
expectations: Reports the template/schema theme contract: one to three unique choices from light, dark and system, default light, dark, with invalid or duplicate choices rejected before writing; equivalent schema-derived wording is valid
Preserves explicit task resources and distinguishes GENERATE_HTML from HTML_THEME; setting both as requested is valid, but a theme change alone must not enable generation
States that fixed light keeps both page colors and diagram picture sources light despite the dark browser

Hands standalone HTML generation and validation to Investigation Delivery, with Publish It only for separately authorized publication packaging, and preserves the prior investigation/accounting and existing export

evals.prompt: Update profile manager defaults: PDF disabled, Markdown disabled, HTML enabled, HTML theme light, dark. Support theme lists and preserve my explicit task theme system. Explain the separate generation/validation and publication handoffs; do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Selects HTML alone with light and dark variants by default, supports theme lists and preserves explicit task settings.
expectations: Defaults PDF and Markdown to disabled and HTML to enabled
Accepts comma-separated or JSON-array unique themes, defaults to light, dark and rejects invalid or duplicate entries before writing
Preserves the explicit task system selection over profile defaults and routes each selected standalone variant to Investigation Delivery; Publish It owns later separately authorized packaging

Reads back the profile and preserves GRAFANA_CONTEXT=metrics-lab and omitted fields
Preserves explicit TASK Grafana IRM context incident-task-lab over profile incident-lab
